base_method_text.title:
Characteristic Guidance: Non-linear Correction for Diffusion Model at
  Large Guidance Scale
base_method_text.summary:
Popular guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) linearly
combines distinct conditional models together to provide enhanced control over
samples. However, this approach overlooks nonlinear effects that become
significant when guidance scale is large. To address this issue, we propose
characteristic guidance, a guidance method that provides first-principle
non-linear correction for classifier-free guidance. Such correction forces the
guided DDPMs to respect the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation of diffusion process,
in a way that is training-free and compatible with existing sampling methods.
Experiments show that characteristic guidance enhances semantic characteristics
of prompts and mitigate irregularities in image generation, proving effective
in diverse applications ranging from simulating magnet phase transitions to
latent space sampling.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper introduces 'characteristic guidance,' a novel non-linear correction method for classifier-free guided Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs). It addresses the issue of irregularities in image generation at large guidance scales by enforcing adherence to the Fokker-Planck equation, enhancing semantic characteristics, and mitigating color and exposure issues without requiring additional training.
base_method_text.methodology: The core of the method involves a non-linear correction term (∆x) applied to the classifier-free guidance, derived by solving the score Fokker-Planck equation using the method of characteristics under a Harmonic ansatz. This correction is implemented through fixed-point iteration algorithms, with orthogonal projections used to accelerate computation and regularize the solution.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: Experiments were conducted on various datasets: conditional 2D Gaussian distributions, a mixture of Gaussian distributions, CIFAR-10, ImageNet 256, and Stable Diffusion. The method was evaluated using metrics like Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and visual inspection. It was also tested on simulating magnet phase transitions using the Landau-Ginzburg model.
base_method_text.limitations: The effectiveness of FID as an evaluation metric is compromised by the difference between the target conditional probabilities and marginal probabilities. The iterative computation of the non-linear correction can be slow, and advanced regularization techniques are needed to enhance the convergence rate and accelerate computation.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring advanced regularization techniques beyond projection to improve the convergence rate of the iterative correction. There is also a need for more appropriate metrics that account for the discrepancy between the target conditional probabilities and marginal probabilities in guided DDPMs.

add_method_texts.title:
Score identity Distillation: Exponentially Fast Distillation of
  Pretrained Diffusion Models for One-Step Generation
add_method_texts.summary:
We introduce Score identity Distillation (SiD), an innovative data-free
method that distills the generative capabilities of pretrained diffusion models
into a single-step generator. SiD not only facilitates an exponentially fast
reduction in Fr\'echet inception distance (FID) during distillation but also
approaches or even exceeds the FID performance of the original teacher
diffusion models. By reformulating forward diffusion processes as semi-implicit
distributions, we leverage three score-related identities to create an
innovative loss mechanism. This mechanism achieves rapid FID reduction by
training the generator using its own synthesized images, eliminating the need
for real data or reverse-diffusion-based generation, all accomplished within
significantly shortened generation time. Upon evaluation across four benchmark
datasets, the SiD algorithm demonstrates high iteration efficiency during
distillation and surpasses competing distillation approaches, whether they are
one-step or few-step, data-free, or dependent on training data, in terms of
generation quality. This achievement not only redefines the benchmarks for
efficiency and effectiveness in diffusion distillation but also in the broader
field of diffusion-based generation. The PyTorch implementation is available at
https://github.com/mingyuanzhou/SiD
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces Score identity Distillation (SiD), a data-free method for distilling pretrained diffusion models into a single-step generator. SiD achieves rapid reduction in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and can surpass the FID performance of the original teacher diffusion models. The method reformulates forward diffusion processes as semi-implicit distributions and uses score-related identities to create a novel loss mechanism.
add_method_texts.methodology: SiD leverages three score-related identities derived from reformulating forward diffusion processes as semi-implicit distributions. It employs a model-based score-matching loss, specifically a variant of Fisher divergence, approximated using Monte Carlo estimation techniques. The generator is trained using its own synthesized images, eliminating the need for real data or reverse diffusion.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The method was evaluated on four benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 32x32, ImageNet 64x64, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQv2 64x64. VP-EDM checkpoints were used as teacher diffusion models. Performance was measured using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS). Precision and Recall were also considered for ImageNet 64x64.
add_method_texts.limitations: SiD requires managing three networks simultaneously during distillation, increasing memory demands compared to traditional diffusion model training. The method also has increased memory allocation and iteration time compared to Diff-Instruct, due to the computation of score gradients.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring the use of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) to reduce the memory footprint of the generator score network and the generator. Additionally, more advanced strategies such as progressively increasing the batch size, annealing the learning rate, and implementing gradient clipping could be explored. Further investigation into reasons for divergence in ImageNet 64x64 training is also warranted.

base_experimental_code:
The repository contains code for implementing classifier-free diffusion guidance using PyTorch. The core components include:

1.  **Scheduler.py**: Implements a GradualWarmupScheduler for controlling the learning rate during training.
2.  **diffusion.py**: Defines the GaussianDiffusion class, which implements the forward and reverse diffusion processes, including:
    *   Calculation of parameters for the forward diffusion process q(xₜ|x₀).
    *   Sampling from q(xₜ|x₀).
    *   Calculation of parameters for the posterior q(xₜ₋₁|xₜ, x₀).
    *   Sampling from the conditional distribution p(xₜ₋₁|xₜ) using the learned model.
    *   DDIM sampling for faster generation.
    *   Loss calculation for training the diffusion model.
3.  **embedding.py**: Defines a ConditionalEmbedding module for embedding class labels.
4.  **unet.py**: Defines the UNet architecture used as the noise predictor in the diffusion model.
5.  **sample.py**: Implements the sampling procedure using the trained diffusion model.
6.  **train.py**: Contains the training loop for the diffusion model, including data loading, model setup, optimization, and checkpointing.
7.  **dataloader_cifar.py**: Defines the data loading pipeline for CIFAR-10.
8.  **utils.py**: Provides utility functions, such as a function for generating beta schedules.

Key functions and classes related to the diffusion process include:

*   `GaussianDiffusion` class in `diffusion.py` which encapsulates the diffusion process.
*   `p_mean_variance` and `p_sample` functions for reverse diffusion.
*   `ddim_p_sample` and `ddim_sample` for DDIM sampling.
*   `training_loss` for calculating the loss during training.
*   `UNet` class in `unet.py` represents the noise prediction model.
base_experimental_info:
The experimental setup involves training and sampling from a diffusion model, primarily on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Key aspects of the experimental setup include:

1.  **Dataset**: CIFAR-10 is used for training and evaluation (specified in `dataloader_cifar.py`).
2.  **Model Architecture**: A UNet architecture (defined in `unet.py`) is employed as the noise prediction network. The architecture's parameters, such as channel multipliers (`ch_mul`), number of residual blocks (`num_res_blocks`), and use of convolution in downsampling (`use_conv`), are configurable via command-line arguments.
3.  **Training Details**: Training is performed using the AdamW optimizer with a cosine annealing learning rate schedule (managed by `Scheduler.py`).  Gradient warm-up is also employed. DistributedDataParallel (DDP) is used for multi-GPU training.
4.  **Diffusion Parameters**: A linear beta schedule (configured in `utils.py`) is used for the diffusion process. The number of diffusion timesteps (`T`) is a configurable parameter.
5.  **Conditional Generation**: Class labels are embedded using a `ConditionalEmbedding` module (defined in `embedding.py`) and provided as input to the UNet, enabling class-conditional image generation.
6.  **Classifier-Free Guidance**: The code implements classifier-free guidance, with the guidance strength (`w`) being a configurable hyperparameter.
7.  **Sampling**: Images are sampled from the trained model using either the standard reverse diffusion process or DDIM sampling for faster generation. The number of sampling steps and the DDIM eta value are configurable parameters.
8.  **Evaluation**:  The code includes an option to generate samples for quantitative evaluation using FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), although the specific FID calculation is not included in the provided code. Visual inspection of generated samples is also implicitly part of the evaluation.
9.  **Command-line Arguments**: The `train.py` and `sample.py` scripts use `argparse` to provide a wide range of configurable hyperparameters, including batch sizes, learning rates, model architecture parameters, diffusion parameters, and sampling parameters.
new_method:
Below is the outcome of step 3—a description of a novel method inspired by both the Base Method and the SiD (Score identity Distillation) approach.

─────────────────────────────  
Title: Characteristic Distillation Guidance (CDG)

Overview:  
CDG fuses the non-linear corrective strengths of Characteristic Guidance—which enforces adherence to the Fokker–Planck dynamics—with the efficiency of score identity distillation. Rather than iteratively computing a non-linear correction term (∆x) during each sample generation, CDG learns a distilled “correction network” offline. This network approximates the fixed-point solution of the non-linear correction quickly in a single or very few forward passes at inference time, thus mitigating slow iterative computation while retaining the beneficial properties of the original characteristic guidance.

Key Steps:

1. Offline Distillation Phase:  
   • Data Generation: Use the pretrained diffusion model guided by the Base Method’s iterative non-linear correction mechanism over a large set of synthesized images (or latent samples) with various guidance scales.  
   • Loss Formulation: Leverage score-related identities in a manner reminiscent of SiD. In particular, design a hybrid loss that combines a model-based score matching term (e.g., a variant of Fisher divergence) with a constraint enforcing that the distilled correction network’s output (∆x_d) approximates the fixed-point correction term ∆x computed via solving the Fokker–Planck equation under the Harmonic ansatz.  
   • Training: Train the correction network in a data-free manner using the teacher’s synthesized images, such that for an input latent sample (and its conditional context) the network learns to output a correction that approximates the iterative non-linear solution. This network serves to capture the inherent non-linear behavior in one (or few) shot(s).

2. Online Inference Phase:  
   • Guidance Correction: At generation time, instead of running several iterations of fixed-point updates, the distilled network provides an immediate non-linear correction to the classifier-free guidance output.  
   • Efficient Integration: Integrate the correction term ∆x_d with the base denoising step, so that the final update obeys an approximated Fokker–Planck dynamics without incurring the computational cost of iterative procedures.  
   • Enhanced Metrics: Since the network is trained to match the behavior of the iterative corrections that are known to mitigate irregularities in high guidance scale regimes, the generation quality—measured by metrics such as FID and IS—should benefit from both rapid inference and maintained semantic clarity.

Benefits and Innovations:  
• Speedup in Inference: By distilling the iterative non-linear correction into a single-step (or few-step) network, CDG substantially reduces the per-sample computational overhead without sacrificing the fidelity of Fokker–Planck conformity.  
• Robustness at High Guidance Scales: The approach preserves the benefits of the Base Method in enhancing semantic characteristics and mitigating artifacts yet avoids prolonged iterative computation.  
• Data-Free Distillation: Following SiD’s paradigm, CDG does not require real-data supervision during the distillation process—only synthesized examples from the teacher model’s diffusion process.  
• Improved Adaptability: The network can potentially be augmented with techniques such as low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to further reduce memory consumption or be refined with advanced regularization approaches that accelerate convergence during offline training.

─────────────────────────────  
In summary, Characteristic Distillation Guidance (CDG) is a novel method that directly addresses the Base Method’s slow iterative computation challenge by infusing the efficiency of score identity distillation, thereby enabling rapid, high-quality guided generation that maintains the theoretical strengths of non-linear corrective schemes.

final_verification_result.explanation: The proposed Characteristic Distillation Guidance (CDG) method innovatively combines two recent ideas: the non-linear correction based on Fokker–Planck dynamics introduced in the Characteristic Guidance paper, and the data-free distillation paradigm from Score Identity Distillation (SiD). CDG proposes learning an offline correction network that approximates the fixed-point solution of the iterative non-linear correction term, thereby enabling rapid inference at high guidance scales. While both individual components have been previously published, CDG’s particular integration—distilling the Fokker–Planck based corrective process into a network to replace iterative computations—has not been directly addressed in prior work.
specific_issues: The idea of offline distillation to bypass iterative computation has precedent in SiD, so the novelty lies mainly in applying it to approximate the iterative Fokker–Planck correction used in Characteristic Guidance.
There might be concerns that the method is an incremental combination of existing techniques rather than a fundamentally new mechanism.
novel_aspects: Offline distillation of the non-linear correction term guided by Fokker–Planck dynamics into a fast correction network.
Data-free training of the correction network using synthesized examples to mimic iterative fixed-point updates, which offers computational speedup while aiming to retain theoretical properties.

major_overlaps: Characteristic Guidance (Zheng & Lan, 2023): Uses iterative non-linear correction aligned with the Fokker–Planck equation.
Score Identity Distillation (SiD) (Zhou et al., 2024): Implements data-free distillation to achieve one-step generation.
minor_similarities: Both frameworks rely on leveraging score-based identities and data-free methods; however, their incorporation with Fokker–Planck based fixed-point updates distinguishes CDG.
unique_contributions: Integrating the distillation of an iterative correction process governed by Fokker–Planck dynamics into a correction network, potentially reducing inference time while preserving theoretical rigor.
Merging the strengths of both the characteristic guidance method and SiD in a novel inference-time strategy.

related_papers.title:
Leafwise cohomological expression of dynamical zeta functions on
  foliated dynamical systems

summary.main_contributions: The paper establishes a leafwise cohomological expression of the dynamical zeta function on a Riemannian foliated dynamical system (RFDS3). It demonstrates that the dynamical zeta function can be represented as a zeta-regularized determinant in terms of the infinitesimal generator acting on the reduced leafwise cohomology, thereby connecting the spectral properties of the flow with cohomological invariants.
summary.methodology: The work employs a combination of leafwise de Rham complex construction, reduced leafwise cohomology via Hodge theory, and spectral analysis of the infinitesimal generator defined through Stone's theorem. It further uses Mellin transforms and heat kernel asymptotic expansions to derive meromorphic extensions and to establish a rigorous connection between the periodic orbit data and the zeta-regularized determinant.
summary.limitations: The analysis is carried out under strong assumptions such as the compactness and smoothness of the 3-manifold, the existence of a bundle-like metric, non-degenerate closed orbits, and finite topological entropy. The results are also restricted to foliated dynamical systems with no fixed points and a finite number of compact leaves.
summary.future_research_directions: Not mentioned as a distinct section; however, future work could explore relaxing some of the restrictive assumptions, generalizing the framework to higher dimensions or more complex foliations, and applying similar techniques to other dynamical systems in arithmetic topology and spectral geometry.

related_papers.title:
SteinDreamer: Variance Reduction for Text-to-3D Score Distillation via
  Stein Identity

summary.main_contributions: This paper introduces SteinDreamer, a novel text-to-3D generation framework that reduces high variance in score distillation by leveraging Stein’s identity to construct flexible control variates. It formulates Stein Score Distillation (SSD) as a general approach that unifies previous methods like SDS and VSD, resulting in improved gradient stability, faster convergence, and enhanced visual quality in both object- and scene-level 3D synthesis.
summary.methodology: The proposed method integrates Stein’s identity into the score distillation process by combining the pre-trained diffusion model’s score estimates with a control variate based on an arbitrary baseline function. In practice, the authors implement SSD using a monocular depth or normal estimator to guide the baseline, and they optimize both the 3D representation parameters and auxiliary variance reduction weights through alternating optimization. This approach uses Monte Carlo gradient estimation with control variates to reduce variance in the distillation updates.
summary.experimental_setup: Experiments are conducted on both object-level and scene-level text-to-3D generation tasks using an open-source three-studio framework as a benchmarking platform. The paper evaluates methods using metrics such as CLIP distance and FID, and includes qualitative comparisons, variance monitoring over training steps, convergence speed analysis, and ablation studies to verify the effectiveness of the proposed variance reduction approach.
summary.limitations: The paper notes that while the proposed variance reduction significantly improves convergence and visual quality, excessive reduction may smooth out some necessary high-frequency details, particularly in background regions. Additionally, the performance of the method may be sensitive to the choice of baseline functions and the incorporation of prior knowledge, and there is a computational overhead associated with calculating and optimizing the control variate.
summary.future_research_directions: Future work could explore alternative baseline functions to further enhance variance reduction, investigate the balance between smoothing and preserving fine details, and extend the approach to incorporate multi-view priors or segmentation information. Research can also focus on integrating additional discriminative or generative cues to further improve the fidelity and realism of generated 3D assets while maintaining computational efficiency.

related_papers.title: Cosmology In Terms Of The Deceleration Parameter. Part I

summary.main_contributions: The paper develops a comprehensive, model-independent framework for understanding the cosmological expansion by expressing various aspects of cosmic evolution—including kinematics, dynamics, and horizon properties—in terms of the deceleration parameter (q) and Hubble parameter (H0). It presents analytical derivations linking the behavior of the scale factor, energy conditions, and cosmological distances with q, and classifies cosmological models (e.g., accelerating vs. decelerating expansion) based on its value.
summary.methodology: The study employs theoretical and analytical techniques, including the Taylor series expansion of the scale factor, manipulation of the Friedmann equations, and cosmographic methods. It uses tools such as Chebyshev’s theorem for integration and derives relations between cosmological scalars (like the jerk, snap, etc.) and observable quantities such as luminosity and angular diameter distances. The methodology also includes Newtonian approximations to study the effects of cosmological expansion on local systems (e.g., tethered galaxies, atomic models).
summary.limitations: The analysis is primarily theoretical and relies on assumptions of homogeneity and isotropy (FLRW metric), which may limit its applicability in inhomogeneous or anisotropic regimes. Some derivations assume simplified models or neglect interactions between cosmic components, and the transition from local Newtonian systems to fully relativistic treatments may involve approximations.
summary.future_research_directions: Not mentioned explicitly, but the framework sets the stage for further investigations into testing general relativity and its modifications using cosmographic parameters, refining dark energy models, and exploring the impact of cosmic expansion on local astrophysical systems. Further observational work is suggested to better constrain the deceleration parameter and related cosmological scalars.

related_papers.title:
Ask, Acquire, and Attack: Data-free UAP Generation using Class
  Impressions

summary.main_contributions: The paper introduces a novel data‐free method for generating Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAPs) by first generating representative 'class impressions' from a target model’s activated memory and then training a generative neural network to craft UAPs. This approach achieves state-of-the-art success rates close to data-driven methods, while also exhibiting improved cross-model generalizability and efficiency.
summary.methodology: The method has a two-stage approach. In the first stage, class impressions are generated by optimizing a random noise image to maximize the pre-softmax activation for a chosen class in the target CNN. In the second stage, a generative model (similar to a GAN generator) is trained using a fooling loss that reduces the confidence of the true label and a diversity loss that encourages variety in the generated perturbations. The network maps latent vectors sampled from a simple distribution to UAPs via deconvolution layers.
summary.experimental_setup: Experiments are conducted on the ILSVRC dataset using standard CNN architectures including VGG-F, CaﬀeNet, GoogLeNet, VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-152. For training, 10 class impressions per class (totaling 10,000 samples) are generated. Success rates are evaluated on a validation set of 50,000 images, considering both white-box and black-box attack scenarios, and comparisons are made with the data-driven UAP approach and the existing data-free method FFF.
summary.limitations: The approach depends on access to the target model’s architecture and parameters in order to extract class impressions. While it significantly improves over existing data-free methods, there remains a small gap compared to data-driven techniques. Additionally, adversarial training only marginally increases robustness, indicating that the UAPs can still effectively fool models even after fine-tuning.
summary.future_research_directions: Future work could explore the extraction of more nuanced information from the target model’s parameters to improve UAP generation further, integrate adversarial generation techniques into GAN frameworks for synthesizing natural-looking data, and enhance defensive strategies through improved adversarial training methods. The exploration of simultaneous multi-model attacks and robustness in real-world applications also presents promising directions for research.

related_papers.title:
Characteristic Guidance: Non-linear Correction for Diffusion Model at
  Large Guidance Scale

summary.main_contributions: The paper introduces Characteristic Guidance, a novel method for non-linear correction in classifier‐free guided diffusion models. It addresses the inadequacies of the traditional linear combination at large guidance scales by enforcing consistency with the Fokker–Planck equation, leading to improved semantic alignment and reduced artifacts in generated samples.
summary.methodology: The approach leverages a first‐principles analysis of the diffusion process by solving the score Fokker–Planck equation using the method of characteristics under a harmonic ansatz. It combines conditional and unconditional denoising networks via a non-linear correction term computed iteratively using fixed-point methods (including gradient descent, RMSprop, and Anderson acceleration) without requiring additional training.
summary.experimental_setup: Experiments are conducted on various settings: sampling from conditional and mixture of Gaussian distributions to validate theoretical predictions, simulations of magnet cooling to capture phase transitions, natural image generation on CIFAR-10, latent space generation on ImageNet 256, and integration into Stable Diffusion WebUI. Evaluations include metrics like KL divergence, FID, IS, negative log-likelihood, and extensive visual comparisons.
summary.limitations: The method relies on the harmonic ansatz, which may not hold in regions with overlapping data or in complex phase transitions, potentially leading to minor artifacts. Moreover, the iterative computation for the non-linear correction can be slow without effective regularization, and standard evaluation metrics like FID may not perfectly reflect the quality of guided DDPM outputs.
summary.future_research_directions: While not explicitly detailed, the paper suggests that further work may involve developing more advanced regularization techniques to accelerate convergence and exploring better evaluation metrics specifically tailored for guided DDPMs. Further extension to broader continuous data types beyond image generation is also indicated as a potential research direction.
